definition: Artificial general intelligence, A concept that suggests a more advanced version of AI than we know today, one that can perform tasks much better than humans while also teaching and advancing its own capabilities.
details: Artificial general intelligence, A concept that suggests a more advanced version of AI than we know today, one that can perform tasks much better than humans while also teaching and advancing its own capabilities.

explainer.lead: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is a proposed kind of AI that would perform tasks much better than humans while also teaching itself and advancing its own capabilities. It matters because it combines superhuman performance and self-improvement in one idea, rather than describing the AI we know today.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helper robot that can solve jobs even better than grown-up experts. Instead of waiting for people to make it smarter, it can also teach itself new skills and improve its own abilities. That imagined helper is AGI, a much more advanced kind of AI than we know today.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, AGI is a target concept rather than a specified tool or implementation. Evaluating a claimed AGI against this definition would require comparisons with human task performance and evidence that the system can teach itself and advance its own capabilities. The concept does not prescribe an architecture, tools, settings, or performance thresholds.
tiers.paperLevel: AGI := a hypothesized AI with performance(task) substantially greater than performance(humans, task), together with the ability to teach itself and advance its own capabilities. The definition does not fix the task domain, human comparison group, measurement procedure, or limits on self-improvement. It specifies a capability concept rather than a model or algorithm.

explainer.example: Imagine an AGI asked to design a more efficient solar panel. It produces a better design than human experts, teaches itself missing science and engineering skills, and uses that learning to improve its capabilities for later design tasks.
explainer.intuition: AGI describes AI with two unusually ambitious properties: doing tasks much better than people and becoming more capable through its own teaching and advancement. The second property distinguishes the concept from a system that merely performs well.
howItWorks: Start with an AI system more advanced than those known today.
Give it a task and compare its performance with human performance.
The system performs the task much better than humans.
It also teaches itself and advances its own capabilities, extending what it can do.
explainer.whyItMatters: AGI sets out a possible future level of AI capability in which excellent task performance is paired with self-directed advancement. That makes it useful as a concept for discussing forms of AI beyond those known today.
misconceptions: AGI is not simply another name for today's AI; the concept describes a more advanced version.
Strong task performance alone does not capture the full definition, which also includes teaching itself and advancing its own capabilities.
